Get a flu shot
The flu is an infectious disease, but it can be dangerous to your health if you have not been vaccinated and are unable to receive the vaccine. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) recommends that everyone get a flu shot every 6 months, preferably before the winter months when the virus spreads more easily. Your doctor will determine whether or not you need to get the vaccine as well as make sure it does not cause any side effects. If you do get sick from a cold or other infection, ask your doctor about the amount of medicine you should take so he knows how much you can safely use. For those who cannot get their shots, there is no treatment needed. You also may want to talk with your doctor about any medications you may be taking and possible side effects.
